meta.title: Solutions — What Forcelis improves
meta.description: Financial performance, operations, supply chain and accounting, analyzed together. Advisory turns findings into decisions; managed services keep the process running.

hero.title: Business performance has no single department.
hero.subtitle: Financial, operational and supply-chain performance are connected. Our analysis is designed to read them together.

detailIntro: Every solution follows the same four questions. Open the one you need.

groups.title: Financial performance
groups.whatItIs: Understand what the company earns, what it spends, where the margin is created and where it is lost.
groups.youGet: A management view of the business that reconciles with accounting, updates every period, and answers the question the P&L does not: which part of the business is actually paying for the rest.
groups.outcome: You know which products, customers and periods make money — and which ones consume it.

groups.title: Operational performance
groups.whatItIs: Find where process, not price, is costing money — and quantify it before anyone is asked to change how they work.
groups.youGet: A prioritized list of inefficiencies with an estimated annual cost attached to each, so the effort of fixing them can be compared against the return.
groups.outcome: Improvements are chosen by what they return, not by who shouts loudest.

groups.title: Supply chain
groups.whatItIs: Inventory, purchasing, suppliers and payment terms are one system. Analyzed separately, each looks fine.
groups.youGet: A clear read on how much cash the operation is holding, where it is held, and which supplier or product line is responsible for the change.
groups.outcome: Less cash parked in stock and purchasing terms, without starving the operation.

groups.title: Accounting & control
groups.whatItIs: Accounting data is the most complete record most companies have. It is also the least used for decisions.
groups.youGet: Fiscal and accounting information restated in managerial terms — comparable across periods, with data quality issues surfaced rather than silently absorbed into the totals.
groups.outcome: Numbers management can trust, because the gaps are visible instead of buried.

groups.title: Advisory
groups.whatItIs: Analysis that stops at the finding is unfinished work. This is where it becomes a decision.
groups.youGet: A short set of decisions with an owner, a sequence and a measure — reviewed against the numbers in the following period rather than filed.
groups.outcome: Findings become decisions that get made, followed and measured.

groups.title: Managed Services
groups.whatItIs: Once a process is defined and working, someone has to run it every month. That can be Forcelis.
groups.youGet: A managed capability with defined scope, methodology and reporting — under Forcelis quality control and a single point of accountability.
groups.outcome: The process keeps running every month without building the team in-house.

note.title: How engagements usually start
note.body: Most clients begin with a Business Diagnostic. It establishes the baseline, shows which of these areas the company actually needs, and makes the scope of anything that follows a matter of evidence rather than a proposal.

closing.title: Not sure which of these you need?
closing.body: That is what the diagnostic is for. It starts from your data, not from a service catalogue.
